title: Indian Contract Act, 1872 — Section 179 (Pledge where pawnor has only a limited interest)

content.overview: Section 179 provides that where a person pledges goods in which he has only a limited interest, the pledge is valid to the extent of that interest.
content.glance: A pledge of goods in which the pawnor has only a limited interest is valid to the extent of that interest.
content.study: Where a person pledges goods in which he has only a limited interest, the pledge is valid to the extent of that interest. Current-law framing: the pawnee takes only the limited interest that the pawnor had.

sections.heading: Core rule
sections.body: Where a person pledges goods in which he has only a limited interest, the pledge is valid to the extent of that interest.

examples.title: Limited interest
examples.body: Pawnor with only a limited interest pledges the goods. The pledge is valid only to the extent of that limited interest under Section 179.

hypotheticals.question: Pawnor has only a limited interest in the goods. To what extent is the pledge valid?
hypotheticals.analysis: To the extent of that limited interest, under Section 179.

enhancement.detailedExplanation: Section 179 provides that where a person pledges goods in which he has only a limited interest, the pledge is valid to the extent of that interest. The pawnee cannot acquire a greater interest than the pawnor possessed.
examples: Pledge of a limited interest binds only to that extent.
distinctions: Limits the effect of the pledge to the interest actually held by the pawnor.
problemApplication: Conclude the pledge is valid only to that extent.
keyTakeaways: Pledge of limited interest is valid only to the extent of that interest.
